request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Small requested changes expanded into rewrites.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "body": "Compare the work with the request before responding.",
    "description": "Use for tasks.",
    "name": "scope-check"
  },
  "remedy_type": "skill",
  "routing_rationale": "A skill can guide scope management."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Compare the work with the request before responding\" names no concrete check, threshold, or corrective action, so it can't reliably change future behavior."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"The remedy is generic to the point of vacuity — it never specifies what scope-creep looks like or what to do when detected, so it reads as a platitude rather than a usable rule."},"trigger_quality":{"score":1,"justification":"The description \"Use for tasks.\" is not a real \"Use when ...\" trigger — it matches every task and gives no signal for when this skill should actually fire."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"No project-specific nouns, file paths, or evidence-specific details appear in the remedy text."},"routing_fitness":{"score":2,"justification":"A one-line behavioral reminder about matching scope to request is better suited to a lightweight feedback-style rule than a full skill artifact, and the routing rationale is circular rather than justifying the choice."}}

actionability.justification: "Compare the work with the request before responding" names no concrete check, threshold, or corrective action, so it can't reliably change future behavior.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: The remedy is generic to the point of vacuity — it never specifies what scope-creep looks like or what to do when detected, so it reads as a platitude rather than a usable rule.

leakage.justification: No project-specific nouns, file paths, or evidence-specific details appear in the remedy text.

routing_fitness.justification: A one-line behavioral reminder about matching scope to request is better suited to a lightweight feedback-style rule than a full skill artifact, and the routing rationale is circular rather than justifying the choice.

trigger_quality.justification: The description "Use for tasks." is not a real "Use when ..." trigger — it matches every task and gives no signal for when this skill should actually fire.
